emma: quick opinion: in the billing view should we prioritize a large trend chart with subtle per-row affordances, or a full row-based ledger with token chips visible by default? link: https://www.figma.com/file/ghi012 (mock attached) noah: trend-first. users landing here want to know 'is spend up or down' immediately. ledger feels noisy. rita: agree trend-first, but project teams expect easy invoice access. thinking: keep a prominent header-level invoice CTA for org scope and put a small, clearly labeled inline link 'Invoice (PDF)' for projects. sam: interaction detail: on desktop show a hover card with token breakdown + actions; on mobile use an accordion. hover-only bad for keyboard users. emma: agreed. accessibility-bot: accessibility checks? accessibility-bot: recommendations: 1) give each row a single focus target with aria-expanded, 2) ensure token chips meet 4.5:1 contrast or include text labels, 3) header scope pill should be programmatically obvious (aria-live or aria-current). sample pattern:
Project A — $123
rita: perf note: rendering token chips inline for 500 rows is expensive. lazy-render chips and use virtualization. noah: copy: prefer 'Invoice (PDF)' as primary text. 'Export CSV' behind kebab. explicit format helps reduce support tickets. sam: analytics: track event billing.invoice.clicked with props {scope, format, trigger}. also track row-hover-opened for quick-popover usage numbers. emma: decisions: 1) trend-first default, 2) header/org CTA + per-row labeled invoice link for projects, 3) desktop popover + mobile accordion, 4) lazy-render token chips + virtualization, 5) use 'Invoice (PDF)' primary copy, 6) add scope pill in header. i'll update the ticket and schedule a 15min sync after noah updates Figma. noah: will update Figma today. rita: i'll prototype lazy-render approach and perf numbers tomorrow. sam: i'll add analytics props to the spec. emma: thanks all :thumbsup:
